# Reproducible beat-grid comparison

`tools/beat_grid_benchmark.py` compares versioned candidate results with
explicitly verified human annotations. Stock Mixxx, this branch, experimental
variants and a pinned Traktor Pro 4 version use the same input contract.
Traktor is a comparison candidate, not ground truth. The tool does not claim
parity from a small development collection or substitute generated beats for
manual references.

The evaluator uses Python's standard library and does not decode, download,
train on, or upload music. Original recordings, annotation files and exported
predictions can remain outside the checkout. Reports include audio identities,
a SHA-256 of the selected reference snapshot and the evaluator source hash.
Selected external annotations are loaded once before evaluating candidates.

## Assemble and freeze the comparison

Aim for 200–300 distinct, representative recordings, including the known
problem cases. Assign category strata for constant electronic music,
breakbeats, half-time, distorted kicks, long breaks, live drums and genuine
tempo changes. Categories may overlap, so category counts are not independent
sample counts. Record sources, remasters and decoder settings; multiple copies
of one recording must not cross the development/holdout boundary.

Keep the existing problem examples in `dev`. Choose a separate, untouched
`holdout` set before adjusting algorithms or thresholds. Do not use the
holdout to tune a phase offset or select a model. Known training overlap with
Beat This! should be recorded in dataset notes and considered when interpreting
generalization. A few supplied examples are not a completed 200–300-title
benchmark.

Manually check the intended musical BPM, ordinary beat lines and bar starts.
Annotate all beats across breaks only when their clock is independently known;
otherwise exclude uncertain regions using annotation intervals. BPM-only
verification is useful but leaves phase, continuity and downbeat accuracy
unavailable. Downbeat labels should identify annotated beat lines. Membership
validation permits at most 0.1 ms representation error, accounting for labels
rounded to a sample boundary while a constant grid interpolates fractional
frames. Labels map one-to-one; their original timestamps are retained for
timing-error metrics. This limit is separate from the 70 ms beat-matching
tolerance and does not shift or snap predictions.

Freeze the manifest revision, reference files, category assignment, split,
candidate software revisions, model checksum, settings, hardware and timing
tolerances before evaluating the holdout. Run cold-start and warm-worker
variants with explicit names/settings, repeat timing measurements, and retain
the original exports alongside the report. The tool does not run Traktor or
extract its grids automatically; an export adapter must preserve its actual
beat positions, tempo zones and timeline origin.

## Decoder timelines matter

The same compressed audio bytes can produce different timestamp origins in
different decoders. For example, MP3 encoder padding may be retained by one
decoder and trimmed by another. A shared audio SHA-256 alone therefore cannot
justify comparing beat positions at millisecond precision.

Each annotation and prediction supplies a `timeline_id`. For a native Mixxx
export, the runner uses `mixxx:<provider>:nativeframes:<sample-rate>` and also
records decoder frame boundaries. A canonical, separately decoded reference
may use a different versioned identifier such as `ffmpeg-gapless-v1`.
When timeline identifiers are missing or differ, beat/downbeat timing metrics
remain unavailable. Explicit scalar BPM comparisons are still possible.
Tempo-zone comparisons also require resolved timelines.

To compare genuinely different origins, independently establish a mapping and
put both `reference_timeline_id` and `reference_offset_seconds` on the prediction.
The mapping is:

```text
reference time = candidate time + reference_offset_seconds
```

The target identifier must match the annotation timeline. Apply only a measured
decoder-origin mapping, not a per-track offset fitted to hide analyzer error.
For a decoder that starts 25 ms later, an independently established mapping
could be `-0.025`. A further 30 ms model error still scores as 30 ms late.
Raw timestamps are checked against the candidate's own `duration` (or
`decoder.duration`) before mapping; the reference uses the manifest duration.
No shift is guessed by the evaluator.

## Manifest format, version 1

Paths are relative to the manifest unless absolute. `duration` is the duration
of the reference timeline in seconds. Audio identity is the original file's
SHA-256. Use actual hashes; the repeated `a` below is a placeholder.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "dataset": {"id": "dj-grid-comparison", "revision": "1"},
  "tracks": [
    {
      "id": "example",
      "audio_sha256": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
      "audio_file": "/private/music/example.wav",
      "duration": 4.0,
      "split": "dev",
      "categories": ["constant", "synthetic"],
      "annotations": {
        "status": "manual_verified",
        "timeline_id": "canonical-pcm-v1",
        "bpm": 120.0,
        "grid_mode": "constant",
        "intervals": [[0.0, 4.0]],
        "beats": [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5],
        "downbeats": [0.0, 2.0]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Annotations can instead live in `annotation_file`, whose JSON contents are
the annotation object above. Do not supply both forms. The evaluator opens
external annotation files only for the selected split. Omit unverified fields;
never use the candidate's own model predictions as manual labels. An absent
annotation or a status other than `manual_verified` produces explicit
unavailable quality metrics.

For variable tempo, replace `bpm` with ordered, disjoint `tempo_zones`:

```json
{"tempo_zones": [
  {"start": 0.0, "end": 2.0, "bpm": 120.0},
  {"start": 2.0, "end": 4.0, "bpm": 144.0}
]}
```

Zones and annotation intervals use half-open `[start,end)` boundaries.
Intervals default to the full reference duration. Gaps in tempo annotations
are unevaluated; gaps in predicted tempo coverage are reported and cannot
count as exact matches. A track can have verified BPM without beat labels.
It can also contain only a verified `grid_mode: "constant"` or `"variable"`;
mode accuracy is evaluated independently and does not invent beat positions.

## Candidate format, version 1

Use an exact software revision or release, plus relevant model, thread-count,
analysis-mode and decoder settings in `candidate.settings`. Predictions for
different software versions must have distinct name/version pairs.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "candidate": {
    "name": "Current Mixxx",
    "version": "exact-git-commit",
    "settings": {"mode": "auto", "constant": "beat-this:1", "variable": "qm-tempotracker:0"}
  },
  "tracks": [
    {
      "id": "example",
      "audio_sha256": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
      "timeline_id": "canonical-pcm-v1",
      "duration": 4.0,
      "status": "ok",
      "grid_mode": "constant",
      "bpm": 120.0,
      "beats": [0.03, 0.53, 1.03, 1.53, 2.03, 2.53, 3.03, 3.53],
      "downbeats": [0.03, 2.03],
      "timings_ms": {"wall": 1200.0, "decode": 50.0, "inference": 1000.0},
      "peak_rss_bytes": 123456789,
      "corrections": {"source": "human", "actions": 1, "seconds": 8.0}
    }
  ],
  "run_measurements": {
    "wall_ms": 1250.0,
    "peak_rss_bytes": 234567890,
    "idle_rss_bytes": 120000000,
    "scope": "analysis-process-and-worker-tree"
  }
}
```

The timings and memory values above are illustrative, not measurements.
Optional stage names include `decode`, `preprocess`, `startup`, `inference`,
`postprocess`, `storage` and `wall`; extra named stages such as
`stream_processing` and `finalization` are accepted. An unmeasured stage must
be omitted, not written as zero. Identify overlapping timing scopes in settings;
the evaluator does not assume that stages sum to wall time. State whether
storage includes the library database or only setting the temporary track grid.

Per-track wall measurements yield explicitly labelled throughput based on
summed track times. They are not the throughput of a parallel batch. Actual
batch throughput uses `run_measurements.wall_ms`, and is computed only when
the candidate's track set exactly matches the evaluated selection. Otherwise
the measured run is retained but its derived throughput is unavailable.
Per-track maximum RSS is reported as the largest observed per-track value;
it is not a sum or a simultaneous process-tree peak. Record RSS scope and use
run-level peak and idle RSS to assess persistent workers and parallel jobs.

`corrections` is optional and requires `source: "human"`. Only measured
action counts and/or elapsed seconds are accepted. Missing effort is
unavailable, distinct from a human-measured zero; no estimate is inferred from
beat errors. Use a fixed editing procedure, blinded/randomized candidate order
and a real DJ setup when measuring correction effort.

Failed analyses use `status: "error"` and an `error` string; omit stale beat
positions. They remain listed as failures. Missing track results are listed
separately. Where verified references exist, missing/failed outputs count as
empty predictions: beat F1 is zero, known beats are missing, tempo coverage
and exact fraction are zero, and a known grid-mode label is not correct.
The absent BPM value has no invented numeric error magnitude. The report marks
these failure penalties, so failing difficult tracks cannot improve average
F1 by excluding them. Unannotated fields and unresolved decoder origins remain
unavailable rather than receiving fabricated error values.
Candidate JSON can reference per-track `prediction_file` objects
relative to the candidate file; external records must repeat the same ID and
audio SHA-256. Unknown or duplicate IDs, identity mismatches, non-finite values,
unordered positions and overlapping zones are rejected.

## Metrics and execution

```bash
python3 tools/beat_grid_benchmark.py \
  --manifest /private/benchmark/manifest.json \
  --candidate /private/benchmark/stock-mixxx.json \
  --candidate /private/benchmark/current-mixxx.json \
  --candidate /private/benchmark/variant.json \
  --candidate /private/benchmark/traktor-pinned.json \
  --verify-audio \
  --output /private/benchmark/dev-report.json
```

The default is `--split dev`. `--split holdout` or `--split all` is an explicit
unblinding action; `all` still reports development and holdout separately.
For embargoed data, put holdout annotations and predictions in external files:
the default run does not open those files. Inline JSON is necessarily parsed
as part of reading its containing document, but holdout annotation and
prediction values are not evaluated by the development run.

| Measure | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Exact musical tempo | Time-weighted absolute BPM error and fraction within `--bpm-tolerance` (default 0.1 BPM); 87 vs 174 is an error, with no octave folding. |
| Grid mode | Agreement with an explicit human Constant/Variable label, using candidate `grid_mode` or the equivalent `constant` boolean; never derived from annotated beat spacing. |
| Beat matching | One-to-one maximum-cardinality matching within `--match-tolerance-ms` (default 70 ms), minimizing total absolute error among equal-cardinality matches. |
| Beat timing | Signed error is prediction minus reference: positive means late. Mean, median, absolute mean, p95/p99 absolute and maximum error are reported only for matched events, alongside missing/extra counts. |
| Grid continuity | Default `--stable-tolerance-ms 20`; a missing beat or an extra predicted line breaks the stable run. Reports stable fraction, longest stable run and longest failure run. |
| Downbeats | The same one-to-one scoring on supplied bar-start labels; absent labels remain unavailable. |
| Correction effort | Human-measured actions and seconds, summarized only over measured tracks. |
| Throughput and RAM | Measured stage coverage, summed-track throughput, explicit run throughput, peak/idle RSS with declared scope; unknown measurements remain unavailable. |

Annotation intervals restrict reference events and false-positive counting.
Prediction collars of one matching tolerance around boundaries allow equal
early/late shifts to score symmetrically. Collar-only predictions count only
when matched to an annotated beat; one global matching prevents reuse where
collars overlap. Stability runs never join across annotation gaps. Near-duplicate
extra lines and all other unmatched predicted lines are counted separately.

Both micro F1 (pooled events) and macro F1 (equal weight per evaluated title)
are provided, along with category and split summaries. Missing references,
missing predictions, timeline mismatches and failed analyses are explicit.
No report awards perfect accuracy to an unannotated track or infers correction
effort from an unavailable measurement. `--include-errors` adds per-match signed
errors for independent plots. Keep tolerances fixed when comparing reports;
70 ms matching is descriptive and is not a claim of acceptable DJ alignment.

The native Mixxx export runner is available in this branch's test executable:

```bash
MIXXX_TEST_BEAT_BENCHMARK_MANIFEST=/private/benchmark/manifest.json \
MIXXX_TEST_BEAT_BENCHMARK_OUTPUT=/private/benchmark/current-mixxx.json \
MIXXX_TEST_BEAT_BENCHMARK_NAME='Current Mixxx' \
MIXXX_TEST_BEAT_BENCHMARK_VERSION='exact-git-commit+settings' \
MIXXX_TEST_BEAT_THIS_PYTHON=/private/runtime/venv/bin/python \
MIXXX_TEST_BEAT_THIS_MODEL=/private/runtime/models/final0.ckpt \
mixxx-test --gtest_filter=NativeBeatBenchmarkTest.ExportSelectedManifestThroughTheProductionDecoder
```

The native runner defaults to the development split and the user's Custom
Models assignment (Constant=Beat This!, Variable=Queen Mary, Auto). Environment
variables with the same `MIXXX_TEST_BEAT_BENCHMARK_` prefix select `SPLIT`,
`PLUGIN`, `CONSTANT` and `VARIABLE`. Decoder metadata describes the actual
production timeline. A stock revision needs an equivalent export adapter or
the same harness ported without changing its analysis algorithm. The test-only
runner and its CMake source entry can be copied into an isolated stock checkout;
it uses the stock analyzer/settings API and omits unsupported downbeat fields.
This portability does not constitute a completed stock-quality comparison.
Results from
different timeline origins still need the explicit mapping described above.

## Measured development controls

The first control batch uses Eurogroove, Apollo Two and Code Red, with the
user's verified scalar BPMs and the existing Custom Models/Auto assignment.
It is a three-recording development experiment, not the planned 200–300-title
corpus. Beat/downbeat annotations and correction-effort measurements remain
unavailable; tempo and mode can be checked without inventing them.

On this cloud x86-64 Debug build with the project's optimization flags and two
Torch CPU threads, three sequential runs per transport used the order one-shot,
warm, warm, one-shot, one-shot, warm. Each run starts its own application and
the first warm job still loads the model. The phase algorithm and input samples
are identical for both transports. All ordinary beat positions, downbeat
positions, BPMs and grid types were exactly equal across all six runs.

| Measurement for the three-recording batch | Per-track process | Reused process |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median analysis-batch wall time | 43.78 s | 38.22 s |
| Observed batch-time range | 43.36–44.93 s | 37.59–42.41 s |
| Median full application-command wall time | 43.93 s | 38.67 s |
| Median summed Python startup time | 5.50 s | 1.82 s |
| Median summed PCM downmix/write time | 0.075 s | 0.073 s |
| Median summed model preprocessing time | 0.431 s | 0.411 s |
| Median summed inference time | 31.94 s | 31.05 s |
| Largest Python-worker RSS high-water mark | 673 MiB | 795 MiB |

The batch median is about 12.7% lower. This is a small exploratory timing
control with visible run-to-run variation, not a representative throughput
claim or a Traktor comparison. The initial single pair (46.35 s versus 38.66 s)
was preliminary; repeated results above are the preferred description.
Worker RSS is its process-lifetime high-water mark, not total Mixxx RAM. A warm
allocator may retain memory across jobs; one process is retained per analysis
thread and the normal completed batch scheduler releases those threads.
Separate 100 ms process-tree RSS sampling was only approximate and can miss
brief peaks or count shared pages twice. It is not substituted for exact
whole-application peak or idle RAM. The native exporter records the narrower
memory scope and leaves unknown measurements unavailable.

Stage timings overlap: `wall` includes decoding, streaming and finalization;
`finalization` includes the worker and grid processing; startup subphases are
included in startup. `storage` is in-memory track attachment, not a measured
library database transaction. The native benchmark isolates beat analysis;
other Mixxx analyzers and deferred database writes are outside this control.

PCM serialization and official preprocessing/resampling are small in this
control compared with inference. No earlier sample-rate reduction, resampler
change or new shared decoder was introduced. Such changes need separate
phase/latency validation. Synthetic cross-rate integration tests confirm exact
one-shot/warm prediction equality at 22,050, 48,000 and 44,100 Hz.

All existing problem tracks remain development regressions. New, previously
unexamined recordings and independently checked annotations are still required
for the frozen holdout, and paired exports from an exact Traktor Pro 4 build
and a completed stock-Mixxx run are needed before judging parity. Beat This!'s
[official README](https://github.com/CPJKU/beat_this) also warns that inference
on its training material can overestimate quality; record known or unknown
training overlap rather than assuming these recordings were unseen.

Run evaluator regression tests with:

```bash
python3 -m unittest tools/test_beat_grid_benchmark.py
```
